name: Lying Floor Cable Curl
description: The lying floor cable curl is performed lying face-down on the floor in front of a low cable pulley, gripping a bar or rope attached to the cable. As the elbows flex, the cable direction from the floor creates a tension curve that emphasizes the biceps in a unique way, with the arms braced against the floor to prevent upper arm movement. It is a strict, low-setup bicep isolation technique.

execution.starting_position: Lie face-down on the floor in front of a low cable pulley. Extend arms toward the pulley and grasp the attachment. Upper arms rest on the floor.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a mat for comfort. Set the low cable pulley. A straight bar or EZ attachment works well.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms extended toward the pulley, upper arms pinned to the floor.
Step 2: Curl the forearms upward by flexing the elbows.
Step 3: Curl as far as possible without the upper arms lifting.
Step 4: Return to the starting extended position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl, inhale on the return.
common_mistakes: Upper arms lifting off the floor
Insufficient cable tension on the setup
safety_considerations: This is a strict, light-load exercise — do not force heavy loads
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full extension to maximum elbow flexion with arms on floor.
